links.comparator_used: Noninterruptive CDS (patient panel icon only, with the same pop-up on hover) in a 1:1 randomized trial
links.outcome: Decision to assess suicide risk in person (primary outcome)
links.effect: 121 of 289 encounters (42%) vs 12 of 307 (4%); OR 17.70 (95% CI 6.42-48.79; P < .001). Documented risk assessment: 63 of 289 (22%) vs 11 of 307 (4%); P < .001
links.tradeoff: Among encounters with a decision to screen, documentation was lower in the interruptive arm (63 of 121 [52%]) than in the noninterruptive arm (11 of 12 [92%]). Authors note alert fatigue as a disadvantage of interruptive CDS, but it was not measured.
links.quote: Accounting for cluster effects by individual clinicians, the interruptive CDS prompted higher rates of in-person screening compared with noninterruptive CDS (odds ratio, 17.70; 95% CI, 6.42-48.79; P < .001), consistent with the study alternative hypothesis.

links.comparator_used: Prior-year baseline (standard of care) rate of documented suicide risk assessment in the same clinics, descriptive comparison; also compared with noninterruptive CDS, both of which used the risk-model trigger
links.outcome: Documented suicide risk assessment rate in model-flagged encounters vs the prior-year baseline
links.effect: 22% (63 of 289 encounters, interruptive arm) vs 8% (64 of 832 encounters) in the prior year; noninterruptive arm 4% (11 of 307), below baseline. Risk-model flagging limited screening prompts to 8% of all 7732 encounters.
links.tradeoff: Benefit seen only with the interruptive display; noninterruptive CDS had a lower rate than baseline. Prior-year comparison was descriptive and non-randomized. No 30-day suicide events occurred in either arm, and the trial was not powered for them.
links.quote: Compared with a study-period rate of 22% (63 of 289) encounters, the same clinical settings had a baseline suicide risk assessment rate of 8% (64 of 832 encounters) in the prior year.

design_hint: interruptive vs noninterruptive clinical decision support alerting
